Thus, we open a new path to investigating these popular open problems in social choice from the perspective of graph theory.

papers.name: The symmetry group of Turk's head knots
papers.abstract: For p, q >= 3 with gcd(p,q) = 1 we show that the symmetry group of the Turk's head knot Th(p,q), the closure of the braid (sigma_1 sigma_2^{-1} sigma_3 sigma_4^{-1} ... sigma_{p-1}^{+-1})^q, is the dihedral group of order 4q. This proves Conjecture R of Di Prisa and Şavk for q >= 3; the case p = 3 is due to Sakuma and Weeks. The argument is diagrammatic: by the flyping theorem of Menasco and Thistlethwaite and Borel's theorem, the symmetries of the hyperbolic knot Th(p,q) are the symmetries of its standard diagram once that diagram has no non-trivial flypes (we write out a proof for the diagrams at hand), and the standard diagram of Th(p,q) has no non-trivial flypes in the sense made precise in the paper (a closely related statement is due to Shimizu, Gill and Joshi) and exactly 4q symmetries. The chirality of Th(p,q) for even p, which also follows from a theorem of Murasugi, is visible in the group. We compare the argument with the geometric one of Sakuma and Weeks for p = 3.

papers.name: The genus of a curve on Calabi-Yau threefolds
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a smooth projective Calabi-Yau variety of dimension $3$, with Picard number one. Let $n$ be the self-intersection of the ample generator of the Néron-Severi group of $X$. Let $\mathsf{GV}_{g,d}$ be the Gopakumar-Vafa invariant of $X$ of genus $g$ and degree $d$. It is conjectured that {\it if $g>\frac{d^{2}}{2n}+\frac{d}{2}+1$, then $\mathsf{GV}_{g,d}=0$}. In this paper, we prove the implication when $d\gg n$ and $X\subset \mathbb P^r$ is a complete intersection in projective space. The vanishing follows by proving that if $C$ is a closed subscheme of $X$ of dimension $1$, arithmetic genus $p_a(C)$, and degree $d\gg n$, then $p_a(C) \leq \frac{d^2}{2n}+\frac{d}{2}+1$. Actually, we prove a somewhat more general result. In particular, we prove that $C$ is an extremal curve if and only if $C$ is the complete intersection on $X$ with a hyperplane $H$ and a hypersurface $F$, namely $C=X\cap H\cap F$. When $X\subset\mathbb P^r$ is not necessarily a complete intersection, assuming that the Picard group of $X$ is generated by the hyperplane section class, we obtain the coarse bound $p_a(C)\leq \frac{d^2}{2n}+\frac{d}{2}+\left(\frac{11}{24}n+4\right)$ for $d\gg n$.

papers.name: On The Manin Constant
papers.abstract: We prove the Manin constant conjecture for every optimal elliptic curve over $\mathbb{Q}$ and Stevens' Conjectures I and II. Our method adapts Hongbo Yin's congruence argument for cubic roots of modular functions to lifts of modular parametrizations through isogenies, using the unbounded denominators theorem of Calegari, Dimitrov and Tang.

papers.name: Adaptive Local Proper Orthogonal Decomposition via Graph Partitioning and Provable Error-Bounded Lossy Compression for Parametric Series in Finite-Dimensional Function Spaces
papers.abstract: We introduce a spatially adaptive proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) method for error-bounded lossy compression of snapshot data in finite-dimensional function spaces. The method combines hierarchical graph partitioning with independent low-rank approximations on spatial subdomains, allowing the local approximation ranks to adapt to the spatial distribution of information in the data. For partitions that are orthogonal in the discrete inner product, we establish an exact decomposition of the global squared weighted reconstruction error into local contributions and characterize the weighted-norm optimality and coefficient-space quasi-optimality of local POD approximations for fixed partitions and ranks. These results provide a rigorous mechanism for allocating a prescribed global error tolerance among subdomains and selecting the smallest admissible local ranks. We further develop a sufficient error bound for the coefficient-space normalized root-mean-square error (NRMSE). A greedy hierarchical refinement algorithm accepts a spatial subdivision only when it reduces the storage required by the local low-rank factors while preserving the prescribed reconstruction-error bound. The method is assessed using synthetic data and snapshot sequences from two- and three-dimensional compressible-flow simulations. The numerical results illustrate how spatially adaptive ranks and partitioning can improve compression relative to global POD and fixed spatial partitions, particularly when the data exhibit spatially heterogeneous dynamics.

papers.name: Off-diagonal hypergraph Ramsey numbers
papers.abstract: For $n,r\in\mathbb{N}$ with $r\geq 3$ and an $r$-graph (i.e., an $r$-uniform hypergraph) $H$, the Ramsey number $R(H,n)$ is the smallest $N\in\mathbb{N}$ such that every red/blue coloring of the hyperedges of the $N$-vertex complete $r$-graph $K_N^{(r)}$ contains either a red copy of $H$ or a blue copy of $K_n^{(r)}$. For every integer $r\geq 3$, we characterize all $r$-graphs $H$ for which $R(H,n)$ is polynomial in $n$. Explicitly, we prove a conjecture of Conlon, Fox, Gunby, He, Mubayi, Suk, Verstraëte, and Yu, that $R(H,n)$ is polynomial in $n$ if and only if $H$ is isomorphic to a subgraph of a lexicographic power of $K_r^{(r)}$. This concludes an extensive line of work initiated by Erdős and Hajnal in 1972 on characterizing the polynomial growth of off-diagonal hypergraph Ramsey numbers.

papers.name: The Hibi--Li (2016) conjecture is fully resolved
papers.abstract: Hibi and Li conjectured that the order polytope $\mathcal{O}(P)$ of a finite poset $P$ has at most as many faces of each dimension as its chain polytope $\mathcal{C}(P)$, and that equality in some dimension $k$ with $1\leq k\leq|P|-1$ forces the two polytopes to be unimodularly equivalent. Fourier proved the inequality in a 2026 preprint. Let $X$ be the five-element poset in which an element lies above two incomparable elements and below two other incomparable elements. Using two results from Fourier's preprint, we show that if an $n$-element poset contains $X$ as an induced subposet, then, for every $k$ with $2\leq k\leq n-1$, its chain polytope has at least $\binom{n-3}{k-2}$ more $k$-dimensional faces than its order polytope, and that for every $n\geq5$ some $n$-element poset containing $X$ attains all these bounds at once. Since Hibi and Li showed that $\mathcal{O}(P)$ and $\mathcal{C}(P)$ are unimodularly equivalent exactly when $P$ does not contain $X$, this proves the equality statement for these values of $k$. The second version of Fourier's preprint gives an independent proof of this statement. For $k=1$, the equality statement is false: the polytopes $\mathcal{O}(X)$ and $\mathcal{C}(X)$ have the same number of edges (Hibi, Li, Sahara and Shikama) but are not unimodularly equivalent. Together with Fourier's inequality, these results settle the conjecture. Our results are formalized in Lean 4, with one result of Fourier's preprint and three published results taken as hypotheses.

papers.name: Forgetting matters: when subspace optimization accelerates without the strong convexity parameter
papers.abstract: Sequential subspace optimization (SESOP) minimizes the objective exactly over a few directions built from past iterates. It needs no problem constants, is accelerated on smooth convex functions and in practice behaves like an accelerated method. This led to the conjecture that it is uniformly accelerated on strongly convex functions as well. The conjecture is false. Consider exact subspace methods whose memory is a window of recent gradients and steps plus finitely many fixed cumulative sums. Uniform acceleration then requires either a window whose length grows as the square root of the condition number or a sum that forgets at a rate of at least the order of the inverse square root. For one filter pair with a fixed factor and a bounded window this scale of forgetting is necessary and sufficient up to constants. SESOP remembers too much and the plane form of conjugate gradients too little: neither is uniformly accelerated, even on infinitely differentiable functions that are quadratic near the minimizer. A short window, in contrast, converges locally quadratically over blocks of steps when the Hessian is Lipschitz near the minimizer and equals a multiple of the identity plus a low-rank term there. Pairs of geometric filters created at fixed times give a uniformly accelerated method with logarithmic memory and no problem constants, also with inexact subproblems. A single pair with a smoothly adapted factor needs two vectors and is accelerated up to a prefactor polynomial in the condition number.

papers.name: Critical orthonormal Strichartz estimates for Lebesgue spaces
papers.abstract: We study orthonormal Strichartz estimates at the critical coefficient exponent $q/2$ for fractional Schrödinger propagators. The proof for $d\geq3$ combines annular Schatten estimates with a frequency summation argument based on potential duality and Littlewood--Paley theory. In dimension two, a trace computation supplies the annular estimate needed for the global estimate. We also construct a counterexample to the global estimate with spatial $L^\infty$ norm and coefficients in $\ell^{q/2}$, even with a weak time norm.

papers.name: Conjugate radius and parabolicity along the Ricci flow
papers.abstract: We study the behaviour of the conjugate radius under the Ricci flow on complete noncompact manifolds. We show that if $(M^n,g(t))_{t\in[0,T]}$ is a complete Ricci flow with nonnegative scalar curvature at $t=0$, the initial metric is parabolic and not scalar-flat, and the Einstein tensor $\mathrm{Ric}-\tfrac12 Rg$ is bounded above, then parabolicity is preserved along the flow and the conjugate radius of $g(t)$ is finite for every $t\in[0,T]$. As an application, we prove that a complete noncompact gradient shrinking Ricci soliton whose volume growth is subquadratic, in the sense that $\liminf_{r\to\infty}\Vol(B(p,r))/r^2=0$, has finite conjugate radius.

papers.name: Deterministic Oracle Complexity for Goldstein Stationarity in Nonsmooth Nonconvex Optimization with Constraints
papers.abstract: We consider the deterministic oracle complexity of finding a $(δ,ε)$-Goldstein stationary point of a Lipschitz function under constraints. Our main result concerns products of convex bodies. Each block contains an inner ball and lies in a concentric outer ball. The inner radii have a common positive lower bound, and each outer radius is at most a fixed multiple of the corresponding inner radius. This class includes common constraints such as balls and boxes. On each prescribed feasible set of dimension $d$ in this class, every deterministic algorithm using a local oracle needs $\exp(Ω(d))$ objective-oracle calls in the worst case at fixed, sufficiently small accuracies $δ$ and $ε$. The objective Lipschitz and initial objective-value gap bounds are fixed, and each constructed function has a global minimizer in the interior of the feasible set. For broader classes of constraints, supplementary results show that every deterministic algorithm needs $Ω(ε^{-2})$ objective-oracle calls in the worst case when $d\gtrsimε^{-2}$ and $δ\lesssimε$. The constants depend on the interior-ball radius and, for inequalities, the local Lipschitz and Slater bounds. These supplementary results cover closed sets that are star-shaped with respect to a ball and convex coercive inequalities with a Slater point, and hold even for convex objectives.

papers.name: An iterated-logarithm price of anytime validity for log-optimal e-processes
papers.abstract: Log-optimal e-variables at fixed horizons, also called numéraires, have been conjectured to ``almost'' form an e-process for exponential-family null hypotheses. A related open question is whether an e-process can attain the optimal e-power at every horizon up to a bounded loss. Given a final horizon, we study the minimax regret of e-processes relative to the numéraires at all times up to it. For the Gaussian location null and the composite alternative of Gaussian distributions with a smaller variance and an unknown location, we show that the minimax regret in the worst case over the location grows like the iterated logarithm of the final horizon. A single e-process attains this rate at every horizon. This growth answers the question negatively. It also refutes the conjecture if ``almost'' means a regret bounded uniformly over horizons. For this Gaussian location problem, we thus exhibit the frontier precisely: the minimax regret is bounded if and only if the alternatives have at least the variance of the null.

papers.name: Additive Relations and Betti Growth in Goldbach Rings
papers.abstract: The binary Goldbach ring over a field $k$ is the quotient of $R=k[x_p:p\text{ an odd prime}]$ by the relations $x_px_q=x_{p'}x_{q'}$ whenever $p+q=p'+q'$, with $\mathrm{deg}( x_p )=(p,1)$. We prove that if $g$ is a map from the odd primes to an abelian group and $g(p)+g(q)$ depends only on $p+q$, then $g(p)=g(3)+\frac{p-3}{2}(g(5)-g(3))$ for every odd prime $p$. This settles Kátai and Phong's conjecture on shifted prime arguments and proves, for odd primes, the affine classification they conjectured for binary sums. The universal group of binary prime relations is free of rank two. We obtain a minimal bigraded free resolution from compatible resolutions of finite truncations and determine the growth of its linear Betti numbers in two regimes. For fixed monomial degree $d\ge3$, as the Goldbach degree $n\to\infty$ through $n\equiv d\pmod2$, we prove $β_{d-1,n,d}\sim(d-1)T_d(n)/d!$, where $T_d(n)$ counts ordered representations by $d$ odd primes. Explicit Koszul cycles from common prime shifts span a positive fraction of this strand. For finite supports $\mathcal{A}_m=\{p\le m:p\text{ an odd prime}\}$, fix the homological degree $i\ge1$ and sum over all Goldbach degrees. As $m\to\infty$, the linear-strand totals are asymptotic to $i|\mathcal{A}_m|^{i+1}/(i+1)!$ when all binary relations on $\mathcal{A}_m$ are retained, and to $(1-2^{-i})|\mathcal{A}_m|^{i+1}/(i+1)!$ when only relations of common weight at most $m$ are retained. These leading estimates are uniform over fields. The interpolation theorem gives eventual depth at most two for the variable truncations; both truncation families have asymptotically maximal projective dimension.

papers.name: The multiplicative complexity of the three-bit low-half multiplier
papers.abstract: We prove that the multiplicative complexity of the three-bit low-half multiplier is six, giving a structural, enumeration-free lower-bound proof valid against unrestricted nonlinear reuse in Boolean XOR-AND circuits. The value was first established by SAT searches of the first author and independently confirmed by the second author. An explicit six-AND circuit supplies the upper bound. The lower bound combines derivatives, quadratic products, complementary minors, and extraction modulo a Boolean ideal. Independent finite checks accompany the arguments. $\mathrm{MC}(M_3)=6$ is fully formalized in Lean 4, using only Lean's three standard axioms (propositional extensionality, choice and quotient soundness).

papers.name: A proof of a conjecture on bipartite correspondence packing
papers.abstract: A correspondence cover assigns a set of possible colors to each vertex of a graph. For each edge, a matching between the two endpoint color sets specifies the forbidden color pairs. A correspondence coloring selects one color at each vertex so that no forbidden pair is selected. A full correspondence packing is a collection of such colorings that uses every color at each vertex exactly once. We prove a conjecture of Cambie, Cames van Batenburg, Davies, and Kang [Random Structures & Algorithms 64 (2024), 62--93]. For every sufficiently large $D$, there is a positive integer $k(D)=(1+o(1))D/\log D$ such that every correspondence cover of any finite bipartite graph has a full correspondence packing if each color has at most $D$ forbidden partners and each vertex has $k(D)$ colors. More precisely, we prove this conclusion with \[ k(D)=\left\lceil\frac{D}{\log D-2\log\log D-6}\right\rceil \] for every integer $D\ge\lceil e^{20}\rceil$.

papers.name: $L$-systems on the large Witt design
papers.abstract: Let $L=\{0,1,2,3,4,8\}$, associated with the large Witt design $S(5,8,24)$, and let $m(n,24,L)$ be the maximum size of a family of $24$-element subsets of an $n$-element set whose distinct members have intersection sizes in $L$. We prove that there are positive constants $c,C,n_0$ such that, for every $n\geq n_0$, \[ cn^{316/63}\leq m(n,24,L)\leq Cn^{169/29}. \] We also obtain similar results for the systems associated with $S(4,7,23)$, $S(3,6,22)$, and $S(3,4,14)$. The upper bounds follow from a non-Shannon information inequality and disprove conjectures of Kupavskii and Terekhov. The lower bounds follow from an algebraic construction for arbitrary Steiner systems.

papers.name: Cycles on the universal moduli of rank 2 bundles over the hyperelliptic locus
papers.abstract: We establish a strong Franchetta property for the universal moduli stack of rank two vector bundles over smooth hyperelliptic curves and identify the image of the Chow ring in the cohomology of a fiber via restriction and the cycle class map as precisely the monodromy invariant cohomology classes. More precisely, for every genus $g\geq 2$, degree $d$, and hyperelliptic curve $C$ of genus $g$, we show that the restriction and the cycle class map identifies the Chow ring of the universal moduli stack with the subring of $H^* (Bun_{2,d}(C),\mathbb Q)$ generated by twisted $κ$-classes, which coincides with $H^{*}(Bun_{2,d}(C), \mathbb Q)^{π_1(\mathcal H_g,[C])}$. We use this viewpoint to give an alternative proof to a theorem of Larson in (arXiv:2404.12607), and verify a conjecture of the second author in (arXiv:2604.11958) in the rank $2$ case.

papers.name: On Primitive Divisor Multiplicities of Lucas Sequences
papers.abstract: Let $(U_{n})$ be a nondegenerate Lucas sequence with coprime integer parameters. Assuming the rational $abc$ conjecture, we prove that almost every index $n$ has a primitive prime divisor of $U_{n}$ of multiplicity one. More quantitatively, the logarithmic contribution of repeated primitive prime factors tends to zero relative to the primitive part along any family with $φ(n) / n$ bounded below, and also in Cesàro mean over all indices. We derive explicit logarithmic lower bounds for Lucas non-Wieferich primes with ranks in prescribed residue classes. Both signs of the discriminant are allowed. Independently, we describe initial multiplicities at good odd primes by a unique Hensel root in the recurrence-parameter disk and by the exact contraction rate of a normalized Dickson-polynomial iteration. Applications include rank and period lifting for Fibonacci numbers and the Wall-Sun-Sun condition.

papers.name: Polynomial twisted periods and affine vertex algebras
papers.abstract: We prove the conjecture of Kang, Lawrie, and Song that Zhu's $C_2$-algebra of a simply-laced boundary admissible affine vertex algebra is isomorphic to the Jacobian ring of an invariant potential obtained by lifting a polynomial twisted period from a Cartan subalgebra via the Chevalley isomorphism. We further identify the $C_2$-algebras of the corresponding Drinfeld-Sokolov reductions with the Jacobian rings of the restrictions of this potential to Slodowy slices. We also extend the Jacobian presentation to non-simply-laced principal boundary admissible affine vertex algebras, where the restriction of the potential to the Cartan subalgebra satisfies a Dunkl-singularity equation with root-length-dependent multiplicities.

papers.name: Kadison's open problem and $R^*$-algebras
papers.abstract: We study $R^*$-subalgebras of von Neumann algebras. In finite homogeneous type $\mathrm I_n$, every $R^*$-subalgebra is locally finite-dimensional. We also give a trace criterion for local finite dimensionality in the semifinite setting under a finite-trace hypothesis, and prove an approximate halving property for projections in strongly dense $R^*$-subalgebras of type $\mathrm{II}_1$ factors. For three projections in an $R^*$-subalgebra of a type $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor, the reduced word-length filtration gives bounds on layer growth, criteria for stabilization, and uniform bounds on minimal-polynomial degrees at each fixed word length. Finally, we give a negative answer to Kadison's fifteenth problem by constructing an infinite-dimensional unital $*$-algebra generated algebraically by three projections in which every selfadjoint element has finite spectrum. The resulting $R^*$-algebra embeds unitally into every type $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor.

papers.name: Beyond Finite Dimensions: Duflo-Serganova Cohomology, the Formal Superdimension, and a Kac-Wakimoto Theorem for Unitarizable Supermodules
papers.abstract: The main results of this manuscript are fourfold. First, we introduce relative holomorphic discrete series supermodules over basic classical Lie superalgebras $\mathfrak{g}$ and $\mathfrak{sl}(n\vert n)$. These are unitarizable highest weight supermodules whose $\mathfrak{g}_{\bar{0}}$-constituents are Harish-Chandra modules of relative holomorphic discrete series representations. We show that these are exactly the unitarizable highest weight supermodules whose globalizations have supermatrix coefficients square-integrable modulo the center. Second, we define the formal superdimension of a relative holomorphic discrete series supermodule as the parity-weighted sum of the formal dimensions of its $\mathfrak{g}_{\bar{0}}$-constituents. We show that it equals, up to sign, the value at zero of an $L$-packet supercharacter obtained by averaging over the Weyl group. Third, we prove a Kac-Wakimoto theorem for formal superdimension: it is nonzero if and only if the highest weight is maximally atypical. For integral highest weights, it equals the superdimension of a finite-dimensional simple supermodule with the same degree of atypicality. We realize these supermodules through derived Zuckerman functors. For nonintegral highest weights, it is computed by generalized Duflo-Serganova cohomology. Finally, to establish the Kac-Wakimoto conjecture, we develop the theory of generalized Duflo-Serganova cohomology for unitarizable supermodules. We prove that the cohomology of a unitarizable simple supermodule is unitarizable and either zero or simple.

papers.name: Large deviations and the asymptotic geometry of Lorentz balls
papers.abstract: We study the uniform distribution on finite-dimensional Lorentz balls $B_{q,p}^n$ in the range $1<p<q<\infty$. We prove a Sanov-type large deviation principle for the empirical measures of the absolute coordinates of a random vector uniformly distributed on $n^{1/q}B_{q,p}^n$. The rate function is given by an entropy deficit under a weighted quantile constraint. We show that the entropy maximizer is unique and characterize its distribution function as the unique increasing solution of a nonlinear boundary-value problem. The limiting distribution has compact support, for which we obtain an explicit bound. These results establish the conjectured empirical limit of Kabluchko, Prochno and Sonnleitner [Journal of Functional Analysis, 288(1):110682, 2025] in the range $1<p<q<\infty$. As consequences, we determine the exponential volume asymptotics of Lorentz balls and obtain asymptotic independence of any fixed number of coordinates. We also prove a law of large numbers for Lorentz norms with finite parameters and use it, together with the volume asymptotics, to obtain a Schechtman--Schmuckenschläger type theorem for intersections of volume-normalized Lorentz balls. We further derive a variational formula for the logarithmic intersection asymptotics. The proof combines an exponential change of measure with quantile interpolation and a variational argument that does not assume regularity of the maximizing quantile in advance.

papers.name: On homogeneous hypertournaments
papers.abstract: Sullivan recently constructed continuum many countable homogeneous $n$-hypertournaments for every $n\ge3$ by forbidding configurations he calls pair-cancelling. We show that, for every family $\mathcal F$ of pair-cancelling $n$-hypertournaments, the class of all linearly ordered finite $\mathcal F$-free $n$-hypertournaments is Ramsey and has the ordering property. In particular, freely ordered $\mathbf{H}_4$-free $3$-hypertournaments are Ramsey, answering a question of Cherlin, Hubička, Nešetřil, and the author from 2021. For every odd $n\ge3$, we give a simple Ramsey expansion with the expansion property for even $n$-hypertournaments by naming an $(n-1)$-hypertournament and a free linear order. We also show that, for $n\ge6$, no unbounded hereditary strong amalgamation class of finite $n$-hypertournaments has EPPA. Moreover, we prove the failure of EPPA for all Sullivan's classes with $n\ge4$, and for the even $5$-hypertournaments. We conjecture that even hypertournaments and classes omitting a family of pair-cancelling hypertournaments, together with the homogeneous cyclic order in arity three, are the only countably infinite homogeneous $n$-hypertournaments for $n\ge3$. We give some supporting evidence.

papers.name: Collapsibility of Vietoris--Rips complexes of hypercube graphs in codimension two
papers.abstract: Shukla conjectured that the collapsibility number of the Vietoris-Rips complex $\mathrm{VR}(I_n;r)$ of the $n$-dimensional hypercube graph at scale $r$ equals $2^r$ for all $n\ge r+1$. We prove the conjecture for $n=r+2$ and every $r$, which gives the first known cases with $r\ge 4$ beyond the cross-polytope case $n=r+1$. Writing $\mathrm{VR}(I_n;r)$ as the independence complex of the graph $H_{n,r}$ that joins two points when their Hamming distance exceeds $r$, we construct a cover of $H_{r+2,r}$ by $2^r$ co-chordal subgraphs. The key general tool is the inequality that, for every graph $G$, the $θ$-number of Bıyıkoğlu and Civan of the independence complex of $G$, and hence the collapsibility number of that complex, is at most the co-chordal cover number of $G$; this strengthens Woodroofe's regularity bound. We also show, using a theorem of Alon, Jin, and Sudakov, that the induced matching number of $H_{n,r}$ equals $2^r$ for every $n>r$, and that $\mathrm{VR}(I_n;r)$ is vertex decomposable if and only if $r=1$ or $n=r+1$. As consequences, we determine the top degree of nonvanishing homology and the coconnectivity of $\mathrm{VR}(I_{r+2};r)$, and we prove split injectivity in top-degree integral homology. Finally, assuming a recent skew Hamming set-pair theorem of Gao and Zhao, we prove that the collapsibility number of $\mathrm{VR}(I_n;r)$ is at most $2^{r+1}-4$ for all $n>r\ge 2$.

papers.name: Creation Sequences for Numerical Semigroups and Exact Counts of Semigroup Partitions
papers.abstract: A numerical semigroup is a subset of the non-negative integers that contains $0$, is closed under addition and has finite complement. A threshold graph is built by adding vertices one at a time, each new vertex being isolated or dominating, and the record of these choices is its \emph{creation sequence}. Reading the creation sequence as a lattice path gives an integer partition and, through the Keith--Nath correspondence, a numerical set in which the dominating vertices are the elements and the isolated vertices are the gaps. We show that threshold graphs with an isolated vertex correspond bijectively to numerical sets, and we study numerical semigroups through their creation sequences. We prove that in the creation sequence of a numerical semigroup of multiplicity $m$ every block of ones and every non-initial block of zeros has length less than $m$, we give criteria for partitions with a unique smallest part and with two distinct part sizes, and we classify all partitions with at most four parts. We show that every partition $λ$ with $g$ parts corresponding to a numerical semigroup satisfies $\ell(λ)\geλ_1$ and, more strongly, fits inside the staircase $(g,g-1,\dots,1)$; equivalently, its creation sequence begins with a Dyck path. Its size equals the genus plus the Weierstrass weight of the semigroup, and asymptotically at most half of all partitions correspond to numerical semigroups. Finally, we obtain exact formulas for the numbers of partitions of $n$ corresponding to numerical semigroups of genus $g$, multiplicity $m$ and Frobenius number $f$, valid in the sharp ranges $g\ge n/2$, $m>n/3$ and $f\ge n-\frac{n-1}{4}$. These formulas solve the open problems posed by Burson, Nam and Sisneros-Thiry \cite{BNS}, recover all of their counting theorems, and correct several of their statements.

papers.name: The Göttsche conjecture and the Göttsche--Yau--Zaslow formula
papers.abstract: The aim of these notes is to give an account, intended for the non-specialist, of the two proofs of the Göttsche conjecture given, respectively, first by Tzeng, and shortly after by Kool, Shende and Thomas. Given a smooth, complex, projective surface $S$ and a positive integer $δ$, the Göttsche conjecture predicts that if $L$ is a sufficiently positive line bundle on $S$, then the number of $δ$-nodal curves in a general $δ$-dimensional linear subsystem $Λ\subset |L|$ is given by a universal polynomial of degree $δ$ in the four numbers $L^2$, $L K_S$, $K_S^2$, and $c_2(S)$. Besides, the Göttsche--Yau--Zaslow formula expresses the generating function of the aforementioned numbers of $δ$-nodal curves in terms of three explicit quasimodular forms and two unknown universal power series, whose coefficients can be determined by recursion.

papers.name: Vanishing geodesic distance phenomenon and boundedness of curvatures
papers.abstract: This article concerns a conjecture proposed by Michor and Mumford in their 2005 paper, in which the vanishing of the geodesic distance is associated to the local unboundedness of the sectional curvature. In this article, we consider a Riemannian Banach manifold with all of its curvature tensors locally bounded. We derive several properties regarding the local boundedness of curvature tensors, and give a sufficient condition for a non-degenerate geodesic distance, which partially verifies the conjecture in its converse form.

papers.name: Projective planes with abelian collineation groups of type (F) are Desarguesian
papers.abstract: We use prime ideal factorization and residue class fields of cyclotomic integer rings to prove that every abelian direct product difference set is classical. This implies that every projective plane of order $n$ with an abelian collineation group of order $n(n-1)$ is Desarguesian, proving a conjecture of Jungnickel and de Resmini. As a consequence, we obtain the classification of circular Costas maps and of Costas polynomials conjectured by Muratovic-Ribic, Pott, Thomson and Wang and by Torres and Rubio.

papers.name: Radial symmetry for the positive Kähler--Einstein Dirichlet problem on the ball
papers.abstract: We prove radial symmetry for every strictly plurisubharmonic function $u$ on the unit ball in $\C^n$, $n\ge2$, that is smooth up to the boundary, vanishes there, and has complex Hessian determinant $μe^{-u}$ for a constant $μ>0$. The known Fubini--Study family therefore exhausts all such solutions. For the corresponding complex Monge--Ampère mean field equation, this establishes the Berman--Berndtsson symmetry conjecture in the smooth class and gives uniqueness throughout the known existence range. The classification also yields the sharp Moser--Trudinger inequality on the ball in Cegrell's finite-energy class.

papers.name: The Singular LeBrun Transform: Complex Conformal and Contact Geometry
papers.abstract: A holomorphic conformal structure is rigid in the presence of rational curves: a complex conformal manifold that is not conformally flat contains no immersed rational null geodesic. So a natural compactification of such a manifold, on which its null geodesics close up, must degenerate along the boundary. We study this phenomenon for the complex conformal manifold that LeBrun attached to a complex contact manifold $Z$ in inverting Salamon's twistor construction: the space $M_{\mathbb{C}}$ of balanced conics of $Z$ transverse to the contact distribution, with its holomorphic Riemannian metric of holonomy contained in $\mathrm{Sp}(n,\mathbb{C})\mathrm{Sp}(1,\mathbb{C})$. Its compactification by the degenerate conics of $Z$ forces the metric to become singular at the boundary. We develop a framework, the singular LeBrun transform, in which these singularities are a source of information rather than an obstacle: the singularities of the metric and of its curvature are read off from the degenerate rational curves of $Z$, locally through the contact neighbourhood of a curve and globally through the incidence variety. As an application, we give an alternative proof of the LeBrun--Salamon conjecture that all positive quaternionic-Kähler manifolds are symmetric, which was recently claimed by OpenAI and by Hu, Liu and Wan. The emphasis of the paper, however, is less on this result than on the framework developed here, which should apply to other problems of the same kind; we conclude with two such directions, negative quaternionic-Kähler manifolds and a singular Merkulov transform for Legendre moduli spaces.

papers.name: The least Carmichael numbers with $k$ prime factors
papers.abstract: Let $S_k$ denote the least Carmichael number with exactly $k$ prime factors. Like the later searches of Pinch, our algorithm builds the prime factors of a candidate in increasing order and stops as soon as the preproduct $P$ satisfies $Pλ(P) > B$. At that point there is at most one possible cofactor, and we recover all of its prime factors at once in polynomial time. We prove an unconditional bound on the number of candidates the search examines, in terms of how far $B$ exceeds the product of the first $k$ primes. When the search is run in doubling passes, this gives a running time of $e^{O(k)} = S_k^{O(1/\log k)}$ under a natural conjecture on the size of $S_k$. We also show that the constant in the exponent is sharp for the set of square-free numbers that the bound counts. Finally, we compute $S_k$ for every $k \leq 64$; Pinch had computed it for $k \leq 35$.

papers.name: Gorenstein toric Fano $d$-varieties have Picard ranks at most $2d$
papers.abstract: We show that the Picard rank of $d$-dimensional Gorenstein toric Fano varieties is at most $2d$. This generalizes Batyrev's conjecture of Picard ranks for smooth toric Fano varieties, which was proved by Casagrande for all $\mathbb{Q}$-factorial Gorenstein toric Fano varieties. The convex-geometric proof is a generalization of Casagrande's proof and Eikelberg's theory of non-$\mathbb{Q}$-factorial toric Picard groups, with key ideas from work of Debarre, Øbro, Fujita and the first author. The proof was found using ChatGPT 6.1.

papers.name: Intersection theory and Chern classes on normal varieties II
papers.abstract: We prove a uniform bound linear in the rank for the local correction terms in the Riemann--Roch formula for reflexive sheaves on normal surfaces over algebraically closed fields of arbitrary characteristic. We also establish the usual tensor and symmetric-power formulas for second Chern characters and prove Wahl's asymptotic Riemann--Roch conjecture and its higher-rank generalization. These results yield second Chern classes of reflexive sheaves on arbitrary normal projective varieties, compatible with pullback by finite surjective morphisms. We characterize their discriminants as infima of normalized discriminants of compatible vector bundles on smooth alterations. As applications we prove Bogomolov's inequality, effective restriction and boundedness theorems on normal projective varieties, a Miyaoka-type inequality, and a Segre-class criterion for bigness of reflexive sheaves on normal surfaces.

papers.name: On Schroedinger operators with subordinated complex potentials
papers.abstract: We disprove a decade-old conjecture about a spectral stability of Schroedinger operators with potentials which are small in a subordination sense. Our counterexample is based on a complex perturbation of a critical attractive square well.

papers.name: Cassini ovals, translated polynomials, and the arithmetic of their discriminants and resultants
papers.abstract: For a polynomial $f$, $a>0$ and $b,ω\in\mathbb{C}$, consider the translate $J^{(a,b,ω)}f(z)=f(z/a)-ωf(b/a)$. We show that for $f(x)=(x^{2}-1)^{n}$ and $ω=\pm1$ every zero of $J^{(a,b,ω)}f$ lies on the Cassini oval $|z^{2}-a^{2}|=|b^{2}-a^{2}|$. We call these translates \emph{Cassini polynomials} and give their zeros explicitly, prove that the zeros for $ω=1$ and $ω=-1$ strictly interlace on each component of the oval, and evaluate their discriminants and resultants in closed form. We then prove the reduced monic polynomials $Q_{n}=a^{2n}J^{(a,b,ω)}f/(z^{2}-b^{2})$ factor into homogenized cyclotomic polynomials, satisfying $\operatorname{Res}(Q_{m},Q_{n})=(b^{2}-a^{2})^{2(m-1)(n-1)}$ for coprime $m,n$, and have discriminants governed by a Lucas sequence. We then prove a comparison principle: if $f$ is even or odd with all zeros in $[-1,1]$, $b\in\mathbb{R}$ and $|ω|\le1$, then every zero of $J^{(a,ib,ω)}f$ satisfies $|z^{2}-a^{2}|\le a^{2}+b^{2}$, and the symmetry hypothesis cannot be removed. As an application, every solution of $\det(A(P_{n})-λI)=F_{n+1}$, where $A(P_{n})$ is the adjacency matrix of the path on $n$ vertices and $F_{n+1}$ is a Fibonacci number, satisfies $|λ^{2}-4|\le5$. This disproves, for every $n$, a conjecture of Gullerud, Johnson and Mbirika that the real parts of these solutions are unbounded.

papers.name: On the Matlis duals of $\mathcal D$-modules in characteristic zero
papers.abstract: Let $R=k[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]$ be a formal power series ring over a field $k$ of characteristic zero, and let $\mathcal D=\mathcal D(R,k)$ be the ring of $k$-linear differential operators. We prove that if $\mathcal M$ is a nonzero left $\mathcal D$-module with $(0)\notin\operatorname{Ass}_R(\mathcal M)$, then $(0)\in\operatorname{Ass}_R D(\mathcal M)$, where $D(-)$ denotes Matlis duality, without assuming holonomicity or finite generation over $\mathcal D$. As a significant consequence of this result, we establish the Lyubeznik--Yıldırım conjecture in equicharacteristic zero. We also obtain a criterion for the Matlis dual of a $\mathcal D$-module to be non-holonomic.

papers.name: Counterexamples to Green's Conjecture via E_6-covers
papers.abstract: We show that curves of genus 10 which are W(E_6)-covers of the projective line provide counterexamples to Green's Conjecture on syzygies of canonical curves. This leads to a 9-dimensional family of explicit counterexamples to Green's Conjecture. We also show that the same curves provide counterexamples to the Green-Lazarsfeld Secant Conjecture. Both Green's Conjecture and the Secant Conjecture are know to be true in the generic case, as well as in many other situations.

papers.name: Möbius-Pseudorandomness for Algebraic Circuits
papers.abstract: We define a notion of Möbius-pseudorandomness for integer sequences generated by multivariate polynomials computed by small and simple algebraic circuits. This mirrors a related definition of Kalai that concerns boolean functions computed by small boolean circuits. We then prove Möbius-pseudorandomness results for polynomials computed by algebraic circuits with few multiplication gates (of any depth), for polynomials with small-dimensional partial derivative space, and for the determinant and permanent. We conjecture that these results hold in general for polynomial-size algebraic circuits.

papers.name: Zeta Functions of Polygonal Numbers: Analytic Continuation, Poles and Zero Scattering
papers.abstract: We study the Zeta functions associated with polygonal numbers, focusing on their meromorphic continuation, poles, residues, and trivial zeros. We then investigate the distribution of their nontrivial zeros. Under explicit hypotheses, we derive an asymptotic formula for the mean real part of zeros in long height windows. The formula predicts convergence of this mean to 1/4 as the height tends to infinity. We also formulate a stronger concentration conjecture and examine numerical evidence for it.

papers.name: Capacities from the Chiu-Tamarkin complex II: Product formula and toric domains
papers.abstract: In this article, we continue our study of equivariant symplectic capacities of open sets in a cotangent bundle defined via the Chiu-Tamarkin complex constructed from the microlocal theory of sheaves. The paper consists of two parts: 1) We develop the theory of $S^1$-equivariant Chiu-Tamarkin complex over complex-oriented ring spectra. 2) Applications of the theory to symplectic capacities: We show that a product formula for the capacities, whose Ekeland-Hofer capacities version is folklore since 1988, is not true via an (uncountable family of) counterexample(s). The counterexample (family) is the product of a concave toric domain of dimension $6$ ($2n\geq 6$) and a $2$-dimensional disk. We also prove a Weyl law of the capacities for all toric domains in dimension $2n$. The algebraic verification is based on a chain model for the Chiu-Tamarkin complex of all toric domains in $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$, which recovers Irie's conjectural chain model of $S^1$-equivariant symplectic homology for star-shaped toric domains (defined only) in $\mathbb{R}^4$.

papers.name: Polynomial bounds for quasiplanar graphs
papers.abstract: A graph $G$ is $k$-quasiplanar if it can be drawn in the plane without $k$ pairwise crossing edges. It was a longstanding conjecture that $n$-vertex $k$-quasiplanar graphs have $O_k(n)$ edges. This was recently resolved by Sadhu and, independently, by Pach, Tardos, and Zeng, based on a theorem in topology proven by Beeker and Lazarovich. These papers showed that $k$-quasiplanar graphs have at most $k^{O(k)}n$ edges. In this note, we greatly improve the dependence on $k$ and show that every $k$-quasiplanar $n$-vertex graph has at most $O(k^2n)$ edges. The proof is based on a geometric charging scheme and Erdős-Szekeres type combinatorial arguments.

papers.name: Siphon faces in slow-fast mass-action networks
papers.abstract: When the species of a siphon in a mass-action network, however many, are fast and their invariant face loses transverse stability along the slow flow, trajectories follow the face past this loss before leaving it. We study three consequences. (i) If the transverse Metzler linearisation is irreducible, the entry-exit relation with its Perron root gives the exit. Under acyclic feeding between its strongly connected components, a max-plus recursion over the reactions gives it; in general neither the Perron root nor the diagonal blocks do. (ii) With one slow species, acyclic feeding and a transversal exit, a fold of the interior critical manifold followed by a drop onto the face gives a unique, exponentially attracting relaxation oscillation whose turning points tend to the fold and exit point. Exactly $3474$ minimal planar networks of molecularity $\leq 3$, with fast per-capita rate affine and decreasing in the slow species, meet our sufficient conditions for it. (iii) A siphon-breaking reaction of rate $δ$ and finite min-plus breaking order $w$ unfolds the transcritical point into a fold if a Perron-weighted second-order self-interaction is positive, and not if negative; the fold's critical component lies at distance of order $δ^{w/2}$ from the face. For $δ=e^{-μ/^Karepsilon}$ the broken face is a floor at $-μ$ in the recursion, and planar cycles leave it between the entry-exit and transcritical points, depending on $μ$. Simulations confirm predicted exits and cycles, including cyclic feeding, where the prediction is conjectural, and high-precision computations confirm the folds; the errors shrink as $^Karepsilon$ or $δ$ decreases.

papers.name: On the toric Bando--Kasue--Nakajima conjecture
papers.abstract: The conjecture of Bando, Kasue, and Nakajima asserts that every simply connected Ricci-flat $4$-manifold that is asymptotically locally Euclidean (ALE), that is, asymptotic at infinity to a flat cone $\mathbb{R}^4/Γ$, is hyperkähler for one of its orientations. A toric ALE instanton is a Ricci-flat ALE $4$-manifold with an effective isometric action of the $2$-torus; such a manifold is simply connected. We prove the conjecture for the toric ALE instantons whose group at infinity $Γ$ is conjugate in $\mathrm O(4)$ to a subgroup of $\mathrm{SU}(2)$: each of them is a multi-Eguchi--Hanson metric with collinear centres. In particular, the conjecture holds for toric ALE instantons with $|Γ|\in\{1,2,3,4,6\}$. The proof uses a closed formula for toric gravitational instantons, which expresses the metric through Hankel determinants of a positive measure on the fixed points of the torus action. With it, the problem becomes a question about lattice points in a parallelogram determined by the end.

papers.name: P = W conjectures for varieties with nilpotent fundamental group
papers.abstract: We prove the cohomological and the geometric $P=W$ conjectures for the moduli spaces of $G$-Higgs bundles and $G$-local systems on any smooth complex projective variety $X$ with nilpotent fundamental group, and any connected complex reductive group $G$. To the best of our knowledge, our results provide the first instances of $P=W$ conjectures beyond curves and abelian varieties. Finally, we provide examples of our theorem for classical groups: as a byproduct of this analysis we investigate when symplectic resolutions of the corresponding character varieties exist.

papers.name: On elliptic curves with prescribed analytic rank at least $2$
papers.abstract: Zywina recently showed that infinitely many elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}$ have rank $2$, settling a long-standing open question. We explore the analytic version of this problem, showing that every elliptic curve over $\mathbb{Q}$ has infinitely many quadratic twists with analytic rank either $2$ or $4$, subject to GRH. We also obtain, under the same assumption, infinitely many congruent number curves with odd analytic rank between $3$ and $17$.

papers.name: Counting Matrices of Prescribed Jordan Type in Incidence Algebras
papers.abstract: We count nilpotent matrices in the incidence algebra of a finite poset over a finite field that belong to a prescribed conjugacy class for the adjoint action of the general linear group. We prove that these counts depend only on the comparability graph of the poset. We introduce shuffle-prefix posets, a class containing all finite interval orders, and give explicit formulas for their nilpotent Jordan counts. These counts are polynomials with integer coefficients in the field size, valid over every finite field. Finally, Fourier duality relates conjugacy-class counts in a coordinate subspace to those in the subspace supported on the complementary matrix positions, whenever one subspace consists entirely of nilpotent matrices.

papers.name: Regularity of Gaussian processes, metric entropy and the Wills functional
papers.abstract: We establish exact relations between three quantities: the growth of the Gaussian Wills functional under dilations, the small-scale metric entropy of the index set, and the critical Hölder exponent of the associated isonormal Gaussian process. For every compact Gaussian-bounded set $T$, the Wills growth exponent $ρ(T)$, the entropy exponent $η(T)$, and the critical Hölder exponent $α_H(T)$ satisfy \[ η(T)=\frac{2ρ(T)}{2-ρ(T)}, \qquad α_H(T) =1-\frac{η(T)}{2} =\frac{2-2ρ(T)}{2-ρ(T)}. \] Thus any one of these parameters determines the other two. Our main tools are a Wills-functional analogue of Sudakov's minoration and a complementary upper bound for $W(rT)$ in terms of local Gaussian widths.

papers.name: Multi-bubble blowup for the energy supercritical Schrödinger equation
papers.abstract: This article establishes the existence of finite time multi-bubble Type II blowup solutions for the focusing energy supercritical nonlinear Schrödinger equation. Given integers $K\geq 2$ and $L\geq 2$, a positive integer exponent $p$, and a dimension $d>d_\ast(p,K,L)$, we construct solutions concentrating at any prescribed $K$ distinct points $\{x_j\}_{j=1}^K\subset\mathbb R^d$, with the asymptotic form \begin{equation*} ψ(t,x)=λ^{\frac1p}(t)\sum_{j=1}^K Q\big(λ(t)(x-x_j)\big)+ζ^\ast(x)+o_{\dot H^σ}(1),\qquad t\to0, \end{equation*} where $λ(t)=t^{-\frac12-ν}$, $ν=-\frac12-\frac{L}{λ_+}$, $s_c=\frac d2-\frac1p$, and $s_c<σ<s_c+\frac{4ν}{1+2ν}$. Here $Q$ is the positive radial stationary profile, $λ_+$ is the slow characteristic exponent in its asymptotic expansion at infinity and $ζ^\ast$ is the limiting radiation determined by the outer profile. The proof combines a matched asymptotic construction of a finite order approximate solution with high order energy estimates and a compactness argument. The key ingredients are the elimination of the self-similar oscillatory branch through a quantized choice of blowup rate and the quantitative control of the combined algebraic tails of the translated ground state potentials.

papers.name: Variationally correct physics-informed operator learning for nonlinear partial differential equations
papers.abstract: Physics-informed operator learning trains neural operators on the residual of a parametric partial differential equation (PDE) instead of labeled solution data, but its reliability depends on a variationally correct residual: one that is equivalent to the error in a norm dictated by the equation, the PDE-compliant norm. For nonlinear equations written as first-order systems, we prove that the first-order system least-squares residual is equivalent to the error in this norm near a solution branch if the linearized residual is stable and the residual derivative is Lipschitz continuous, possibly in a norm stronger than the error norm. We verify these conditions for monotone reaction, solution- and gradient-dependent diffusion, and compressible Neo-Hookean hyperelasticity. The stability mechanisms vary across these classes, as do the regions where the equivalence holds, from arbitrary bounded sets to a neighborhood of the branch. In a conforming finite element space, we show that the loss excess of a state near the finite element solution is equivalent to its squared distance from that solution. We use this loss to train a reduced basis neural operator with values in this space, with solution snapshots needed only for the basis and the loss and its symbolically derived gradient assembled by the finite element library. At inference, this loss estimates the error. Numerically, the square root of the loss excess tracks the error within factors comparable to those of the linear case, and the operator achieves higher accuracy in the PDE-compliant norm than grid-based baselines evaluated in the same finite element space.

papers.name: A proof of the Reinhardt conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove the Reinhardt conjecture: among centrally symmetric convex disks in the plane, the smoothed regular octagon has the least optimal lattice packing density, and equality holds precisely for its nonsingular affine images. The proof combines explicit bounds on the number of control arcs, local cost inequalities and rigorous finite verification of the remaining switching types.

papers.name: Sharp High-Dimensional Gaussian Approximations over Rectangles without Covariance Restrictions
papers.abstract: We study how well a sum of $n$ independent random vectors with $p$ coordinates can be approximated by a Gaussian vector with the same mean and covariance. We measure the error over rectangles, so the bounds apply to maxima and simultaneous confidence regions. The coordinates may be arbitrarily dependent, even exactly linearly dependent, and the bounds do not deteriorate as the covariance matrix becomes singular. After standardizing the coordinate variances, bounded or sub-exponential coordinates give the $n^{-1/2}$ sample-size rate up to logarithmic factors, with the size or tail bounds held fixed. The main upper bounds retain the Gaussian expected maximum, improving the rates when the coordinates are strongly dependent. Fourth-moment refinements give further improvements when large observations contribute little to individual coordinate variances. If we instead impose a fixed moment bound of order $q>4$ on the largest absolute coordinate, together with a coordinate fourth-moment bound, the rate becomes $n^{-1/2+1/q}$ up to logarithmic factors. At $q=4$, the slower $n^{-1/4}$ rate is unavoidable, confirming our earlier conjecture. We also allow the bounds on observation size to grow with $n$. Lower-bound examples show that the dependence on sample size, observation size, and Gaussian width is sharp up to logarithmic factors in the regimes studied, and in several regimes the upper and lower bounds match including the logarithmic terms.

papers.name: Ice and mirrors
papers.abstract: Given a mirror pair of smooth affine principal upper cluster varieties admitting reddening sequences, we show that homological mirror symmetry for principal cluster varieties -- assumed compatible with certain cluster structures -- descends under freezing. This allows us to induct on the following class. A skew-symmetrizable matrix is peelable if, by mutations and removing sinks or sources, it can be reduced to the empty matrix; it is sub-peelable if it is a principal submatrix of a peelable matrix. We establish homological mirror symmetry for full rank upper cluster varieties whose mutable matrix is sub-peelable. We show sub-peelability for the Fock--Goncharov SL(n) quiver for any compact surface with nonempty boundary, all of whose boundaries have markings. Consequently, we establish homological mirror symmetry between the moduli of decorated SL(n) local systems and the corresponding pinned PGL(n) spaces. The results were obtained using ChatGPT Astra.

papers.name: Expansion in powers of simple groups of Lie type
papers.abstract: We prove an expansion theorem for direct powers of all nonabelian finite simple groups $G$ other than the alternating groups and the Suzuki groups ${}^2B_2(q)$. If $G^m$ is generated by $d\ge2$ elements, then $G^m$ has a symmetric generating multiset of at most $Cd$ elements and normalized spectral gap at least $C^{-1}d^{-\log_2 3}$, for an absolute constant $C>0$. In particular, this answers a question of Sabatini on $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{F}_p)^p$. For $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{F}_q)$, we use the expander graphs constructed by Lubotzky--Samuels--Vishne, and an amplification trick for direct powers; in high rank, we use the Ershov--Jaikin-Zapirain property (T) theorem.

papers.name: A Counterexample to Voiculescu's Normal Dilation Conjecture
papers.abstract: We construct a compact operator $T$ with trace class self-commutator and vanishing Helton-Howe measure such that $T\oplus S-M\notin \mathcal{S}_2$ for every bounded operator $S$ and every bounded normal operator $M$. This gives counterexamples to Voiculescu's normal dilation and stable classification conjectures. The construction uses magnetic shifts on finite square tori. Their real parts have commutators of uniformly bounded trace norm, while their frame errors admit logarithmic lower bounds in the lattice size. A summability criterion for frame error turns these finite-dimensional estimates into a compact counterexample. The same operator inequalities yield a rank profile invariant under Hilbert-Schmidt perturbations and normal stabilization, which distinguishes the example from zero.

papers.name: Cantor Julia sets of positive area in non-autonomous dynamics
papers.abstract: For every $a>0$, we prove the existence of a sequence of polynomials with rational coefficients whose non-autonomous iteration produces a Julia set of planar area $a$. We also construct a sequence of rational maps with rational coefficients whose Julia set has the same prescribed area. No individual map in this rational sequence is Möbius-conjugate to a polynomial, and no choice of Möbius coordinates at successive phases turns it into a polynomial sequence. In both cases, for every $n\geq1$, the Julia set obtained by starting the iteration at the $n$-th map, called the phase-$n$ Julia set, is a Cantor set and meets every neighborhood of each of its points in positive planar area. For every $A\in(0,1)$, we construct two sequences of quadratic polynomials, each with $\infty$ in every phase Julia set and with first phase Julia set of normalized spherical area $A$. In one sequence, every phase Julia set is a Cantor set of locally positive spherical area. In the other, every phase Julia set has countably infinitely many connected components and equals the closure of its interior. Both sequences admit invariant measurable line fields whose essential supports are the corresponding phase Julia sets. Finally, for every $d\in[0,2]$, we construct a sequence of quadratic polynomials for which every phase Julia set is a Cantor set of zero spherical area with local Hausdorff dimension $d$ at each of its points.

papers.name: Singular sets of conformal curves are discrete
papers.abstract: We prove that the differential of a non-constant conformal curve between Euclidean spaces has full rank outside a discrete set. In particular, conformal curves are real-analytic outside a discrete set. We provide examples of entire associative and coassociative conformal curves with a non-empty singular set. We show that every non-constant Special Lagrangian conformal curve is a real-analytic conformal immersion. We also prove that a non-constant conformal curve has discrete fibers.

papers.name: Generic splitting types and Terao's conjecture for seventeen and eighteen lines
papers.abstract: We prove that the generic splitting type of the logarithmic bundle of an arrangement of at most eighteen lines in the complex projective plane is determined by the intersection lattice. In particular, Terao's freeness conjecture holds for seventeen and eighteen lines. For any number of lines, it holds for free arrangements whose smaller exponent is at most eight. By the theorem for at most sixteen lines, the problem reduces to a uniformity condition for lattices of seventeen lines: if all realizations have minimal Jacobian-syzygy degree at least seven, then all or none have degree seven. The proof has two parts. First, a realization of minimal degree seven has defect at most four, the defect being the length of the zero scheme of a minimal section. This uses the residual inflection quartic of the associated degree-seven foliation, local inflection identities, and fixed-point theory for critically fixed rational maps of degree seven with exact finite certificates. Second, the uniformity condition holds at these defects. For multiplicities at most six, a critical realization contains a twelve-line core of minimal weight, and an exact search through extensions of the cores shows that the lattice has a single Galois orbit of realizations; the only family left at defect four has no critical member. For a point of multiplicity seven we use the zero scheme of the pencil derivation and a classification of transversal structures. Terao's conjecture for seventeen and eighteen lines needs only defects one, two and three and, for seventeen lines, this classification at multiplicity seven. The proof is computer-assisted.

papers.name: Melnikov residuals and stationary amalgamation in PAC fields
papers.abstract: We construct an invariant symmetric ternary relation with existence and stationarity over models for classes of characteristic-zero Frobenius fields associated with Melnikov formations. For proper formations, the automorphism theories of their canonical root-predicate expansions have amalgamation and no model companion. The underlying fields are then unbounded, and their theories are NSOP$_1$ but not simple. In this case, on triples of elementary submodels, the constructed relation implies ordinary nonforking, which implies Kim-independence, which implies linear disjointness; all three implications are strict. We also study p.e.c. fields with group actions, namely fields existentially closed in every regular extension carrying an extension of the action. We prove that the class of p.e.c.\ difference fields of characteristic zero is not elementary, and that the theory of all characteristic-zero difference fields with canonical root predicates has no model companion.

papers.name: Almost Controlled: The FDR of Benjamini-Hochberg on Weighted Conformal p-Values
papers.abstract: Weighted conformal p-values generalize conformal inference to cases with covariate shift. One way to use them is to pass them to the Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) procedure, either to decide which test units to select or to detect outliers. But weighted conformal p-values may not be positively dependent, so we want to know: does BH still control the false discovery rate (FDR) in finite samples? Based on experiments, it appears to, but we prove it doesn't. We give two counterexamples, certified in exact rational arithmetic, where the FDR exceeds its target level $q$. We also identify how large the difference between the FDR and $q$ can be. With $n$ calibration points, $m$ test units and weight ratio $B$, the relative excess $\mathrm{FDR}/q-1$ is bounded by a function of $n$, $m$, $B$ and $q$ that is of order $\sqrt{Bm/(nq)}$ when $Bm/(nq)$ is small. The bound holds for every configuration with $B\le n$ and every $n$. This order can be reached when multiple non-null test units share a common threshold: in a Poisson-limit model, that configuration's excess is $c(q)\sqrt{Bm/(nq)}$ to first order as $B/n\to0$ and then $m\to\infty$. For some fixed distributions with this structure, the excess decreases only like $n^{-1/2}$ as $n$ grows. If every test unit is null, the excess is $O(B/n)$ at fixed $m$, and in certain configurations it grows linearly with $m$. To assist practitioners in judging how large the FDR can be, we turn that bound, which depends only on $n$, $m$, $q$ and $B$, into a lowered BH level with proved finite-sample control, and give a much less conservative rule of thumb that covers every worst case we were able to find but provides no guarantee.

papers.name: A Scalable Decentralized Event-Triggered Topology-Switching Protocol for Verifiable Safety in Multi-Agent Systems
papers.abstract: This paper develops a decentralized event-triggered topology-switching protocol that allows agents to disconnect from the communication network while preserving state safety and excluding Zeno behavior. We establish a robust barrier function condition that guarantees safety as long as the estimation error remains within a prescribed threshold. Each agent uses locally computable certificates to determine when to connect and disconnect from the network. The certificate construction improves scalability by reducing the complexity of topology-dependent computations from $O(2^N)$ to $O(N)$, where $N$ is the number of agents. We formally prove that the protocol ensures the estimation error does not exceed the prescribed threshold and is non-Zeno. An alternating method computes an error-weighting matrix and a quadratic barrier function that guarantee safety under the proposed protocol. Finally, we evaluate the protocol on four interconnected microgrids. Compared with maintaining network connectivity at all times, the protocol reduces the time agents remain connected while keeping phase and frequency within their safe operating region.

papers.name: Crossing Numbers of Complete Graphs: the independent odd crossing number
papers.abstract: We show that the Harary--Hill bound on the crossing number of complete graphs as well as the Zarankiewwicz bound on the crossing number of complete bipartite graphs, both recently established by OpenAI, also hold for the independent odd crossing number. This implies that the same bounds hold for several other crossing number variants such as the (independent) algebraic crossing number and the (independent) pair crossing number.

papers.name: On $U(1)^{2}$-Invariant Cayley $4$-Folds in $\mathbb{R}^{8}$
papers.abstract: We study $ \mathrm{U}(1) $-invariant Cayley submanifolds in $ \mathbb{R}^{8} $, under the action with weights $ (e^{i θ_{1}}, e^{i θ_{2}}, e^{-i(θ_{1} + θ_{2})}, 1) $ on coordinates $ (z_{1}, z_{2}, z_{3}, z_{4}) \in \mathbb{C}^{4} $. Locally, we can prove that $ N $ can be written as a graph of functions $ u, v, a_{1}, a_{2}: \mathbb{R}^{2} \rightarrow \mathbb{R} $ (where $ a_{3}= -a_{1}-a_{2} $), where unlike in the special Lagrangian setting, the moment-map parameters are not required to be constant, which gives rise to additional degrees of freedom in the reduced equations. We prove that $ N $ is Cayley if and only if a non-linear, Cauchy-Riemann system of partial differential equations in $ u, v, a_{1}, a_{2} $ holds, with ellipticity away from its degeneracy locus. We investigate the special Lagrangian and coassociative reductions of the system, obtaining potential functions in both cases. For general $ \mathrm{U}(1)^{2} $-invariant Cayley $ 4 $-folds, we derive almost-conservation laws (with clear obstruction terms) involving natural $ S_{3} $-invariant and alternating combinations of the moment-map parameters. These identities exhibit additional source terms, distinguishing the general Cayley system from its special Lagrangian and coassociative reductions.

papers.name: Mean curvature flow into an ambient Riemannian manifold evolving by Ricci-Bourguignon flow
papers.abstract: We study the mean curvature flow in Riemannian manifolds evolving by the Ricci-Bourguignon flow. Using DeTurck's trick, we establish short-time existence and uniqueness for the mean curvature flow in this time-dependent ambient geometry. In the case where the ambient metric evolves by a self-similar solution to the Ricci-Bourguignon flow, we characterize the associated mean curvature solitons and derive a Huisken monotonicity-type formula adapted to the Ricci-Bourguignon setting. As a consequence, we show that, in compact ambient manifolds, type-I singularities of the mean curvature flow in a gradient shrinking Ricci-Bourguignon soliton background have, after suitable parabolic rescaling, weighted minimal hypersurfaces as their limiting models, while in the noncompact setting, we establish the corresponding result for a gradient shrinking Schouten soliton background. This provides a geometric framework for understanding how the ambient scalar curvature influences the formation and structure of singularity models for the mean curvature flow. We also show how to construct explicit examples of mean curvature flow in a gradient Ricci-Bourguignon soliton background.

papers.name: Second-Order Cone Valid Inequalities for Set-Point Tracking with Energy Storage
papers.abstract: Convex relaxations of energy storage models drop the complementarity constraints that forbid simultaneous charging and discharging. In the set-point tracking problem, the relaxation can then charge and discharge simultaneously at no cost, as the tracking error depends only on the net power of the storage. We show that the convex hull of the single-period epigraph of the tracking error, under complementarity, is the epigraph of a parabolic cylinder. The resulting second-order cone inequality adds to the tracking error a penalty on the product of the charging and discharging powers and is the tightest convex member of the pencil of quadrics through the two branches of the epigraph. With power limits and the mode variable, the hull is given by the perspective reformulation of the two modes, which dominates the cylinder. In 20000 instances, the cylinder reduces the hours with simultaneous charging and discharging by more than 99% and yields an optimal schedule in 98.8% of them.

papers.name: On the Starshapedness of the Symmetrized Bidisc
papers.abstract: It is well known that the symmetrized bidisc $\mathbb{G}_2$ is star-like about the point $(0,0)$. In our attempt to check if there are other points about which $\mathbb{G}_2$ is star-like, we find that $\mathbb{G}_2$ cannot be starlike about any point $(s,p)\neq(0,0)\in \mathbb{G}_2$.

papers.name: Exploring Low-Regret Energy System Transition Pathways with Modeling to Generate Alternatives
papers.abstract: Long-term planning of energy system transitions is complex due to interdependent investment decisions and uncertain market and policy conditions. Stochastic optimization models account for this uncertainty by identifying a single optimal hedging strategy. However, the flexibility in technology choice and investment timing, i.e., the transition flexibility, usually remains unexplored. Modeling to generate alternatives (MGA) explores near-optimal solution spaces but has not been coupled with stochastic optimization to quantify the transition flexibility. We explore the low-regret pathway space, i.e., all transition pathways that stay within a chosen regret tolerance in every scenario. We introduce a termination criterion for MGA that bounds the exploration error in high-dimensional solution spaces and measure how far each pathway decision, once taken, narrows the capacity ranges of the others. We apply the method to an industrial energy system in Germany. The pathway that minimizes the worst-case regret keeps it at 2.2%, compared with up to 30.9% for perfect-foresight pathways. The transition flexibility increases most at low regret tolerances. At 3.5%, the capacity ranges are on average about 60% as wide as at the highest regret tolerance of 10%. A large share of these capacity ranges is surplus capacity, i.e., capacity installed in addition to, not instead of, other capacity. Surplus capacity is largely not operated but, once installed, narrows the other capacity ranges more strongly than operated capacity. Exploring the low-regret pathway space, rather than reporting a single optimal pathway, therefore is the more informative basis for planning energy system transitions under uncertainty.

papers.name: The Sum of Leaf Weights in the Minimum Spanning Tree of the Complete Graph
papers.abstract: Let $G_n$ be a random weighted complete graph on $n$ vertices, where edges have i.i.d. $\text{Unif}(0,1)$ weights. Let $T_n$ be the Minimum Spanning Tree (MST) of $G_n$. The expected weight of $T_n$ is known to converge to $ζ(3) = \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{k^3}$ (Frieze 1985). We investigate the sum of weights of edges incident to the leaves of $T_n$, denoting this quantity by $L_n$. We give tight upper and lower bounds on $\mathbb{E}[L_n]$ and determine its limit as $n$ diverges, leveraging typical behavior of sparse Erdős--Rényi random graphs. We also establish concentration of $L_n$ around $\mathbb{E}[L_n]$ and almost sure convergence to this value. These results directly yield substantial improvements to state-of-the-art bounds for two important variants of the MST problem: (1) an improved upper bound on the weight of the optimal random instance Steiner tree, as studied by Bollobás, Gamarnik, Riordan, and Sudakov (2004); and (2) an improvement over the upper bound for the Probabilistic Minimum Spanning Tree, introduced by Bertsimas (1988).

papers.name: The cost of enforcing long-run coverage: a phase transition in online conformal prediction
papers.abstract: Consider an online prediction setting, where at each time, we are given a new feature vector and asked to provide a prediction interval or prediction set that will likely contain the corresponding response. In this setting, if the data points are i.i.d. (or more generally, exchangeable), conformal prediction provides a mechanism for building valid prediction sets around the output of any trained model, offering coverage probability $\geq 1-α$ at each time $t$. In practice, however, issues such as distribution drift, changepoints, or other challenges may cause violations of the i.i.d. assumption. In this adversarial setting, online conformal prediction methods can still offer guarantees on long-run empirical coverage. However, there is a trade-off between these two types of goals: enforcing tight constraints on long-run empirical coverage to protect against the adversarial setting can lead to unstable oscillations in the instantaneous training-conditional coverage in the i.i.d. setting. In this work, we seek best-of-both-worlds algorithms that aim to minimize cumulative error in instantaneous training-conditional coverage when in the i.i.d. setting, while also offering long-run empirical coverage guarantees in the adversarial setting. Specifically, consider a condition that requires long-run empirical coverage to deviate from the target level $1-α$ by at most $\mathcal{O}(T^{-β})$, for some $β\in[0,1]$. We prove that this family of conditions can be described with a phase transition. For $β\in[0,\frac{1}{2}]$, it is possible to construct algorithms satisfying such a constraint in the adversarial setting, while offering the same instantaneous coverage performance as split conformal prediction if the data is in fact i.i.d. On the other hand, for $β\in(\frac{1}{2},1]$, this type of condition comes at a cost, and does not achieve best-of-both-worlds behavior.

papers.name: Large gaps and the ten martini problem for monotone quasiperiodic Schrödinger operators
papers.abstract: We prove the ten martini theorem for a large class of monotone potentials. The key strategy is to establish polynomially large gaps for periodic approximations.

papers.name: Axioms for relative entropy
papers.abstract: For normal states of arbitrary von Neumann algebras, we characterize positive finite multiples of Araki relative entropy among non-degenerate divergences. The axioms are monotonicity under normal unital completely positive maps, tensor additivity, superadditivity for product second states, and separate lower semicontinuity in the predual norm. Alternatively, a conditional-expectation identity replaces the two tensor assumptions. The proof uses order bounds and asymptotic estimates on tensor powers. An appendix proves the known analytic estimates needed here, using standard modular theory and Haagerup L^p spaces. We also obtain the corresponding characterization in the C* algebraic setting.

papers.name: Complex Moments of the Derivative of the Riemann Zeta Function
papers.abstract: We investigate the complex moments of the derivative of the Riemann zeta function through a random Euler product model. For each fixed $σ>1/2$ and every $s\in\mathbb{C}$ with $\operatorname{Re}(s)>0$, we show, under the Lindelöf hypothesis, that the $2s$-th moment of $|ζ'(σ+\mathrm{i}t)|$ over $t\in[1,T]$ converges, as $T\to\infty$, to the corresponding moment of the derivative of the random Euler product. We then establish, unconditionally, an asymptotic formula for the latter moment as $σ\downarrow 1/2$ throughout the half-plane $\operatorname{Re}(s)>0$. For positive real moments, our approach is based on a change-of-measure argument and a Gaussian limit theorem for the logarithmic derivative under a tilted probability measure. For general complex moments, we combine Fourier analysis of weighted complex measures with regularized Riesz distributions. As an application, under the Lindelöf hypothesis, we resolve the conjecture of Simm and Wei [J. Lond. Math. Soc. 113 (2026)] on the complex moments of the derivative of the Riemann zeta function for every $s\in\mathbb C$ with $\operatorname{Re}(s)>0$. We establish the predicted asymptotic formula as $σ\downarrow1/2$, with the leading order $s^2+2s$ and an explicit leading coefficient involving an arithmetic factor and the confluent hypergeometric function of the first kind. The conjecture also holds unconditionally when $\operatorname{Re}(s)\in (0,2)$.

papers.name: Regular subgroups of wreath products and Cayley Cartesian products
papers.abstract: The Cartesian product of Cayley graphs is again a Cayley graph. For connected graphs, the converse question reduces to Cartesian powers of Cartesian-prime graphs, and consequently to the study of regular subgroups of wreath products in the product action. We prove that, for a transitive permutation group $G$ of degree $2p$ or $4p$, where $p$ is prime, $G\wr S_2$ contains a regular subgroup if and only if $G$ does, and construct counterexamples of degree $8p$ for every prime $p\equiv3\pmod4$. By modifying this construction, we obtain an infinite family of connected non-Cayley graphs whose Cartesian squares are Cayley graphs, giving a negative answer to the converse question. The smallest graph in our family has $120$ vertices and valency $27$. In contrast, we prove that a connected vertex-transitive graph of order $pq$, where $p$ and $q$ are primes, has a Cayley Cartesian power if and only if the graph itself is Cayley.

papers.name: Random compositions of quasiperiodic cocycles
papers.abstract: We consider the multiplicative process given by random compositions of linear cocycles over toral translations. Under appropriate generic assumptions, we establish effective large deviations estimates as well as the Hölder continuity of the associated Lyapunov exponent of the process. These properties in particular show the regularizing effect of randomness on quasiperiodic dynamics. The novelty of our approach allows for the study of such properties notwithstanding the lack of a spectral gap for the corresponding transition operator.

papers.name: Second scaling regime in high-dimensional function approximation and curse of dimensionality
papers.abstract: High-dimensional function approximation is often subject to the curse of dimensionality, commonly described by a hypercube scaling regime with a large expense of $R^d$ grid points, where $R$ denotes the side length of a hypercube in $d$ dimensions. Here we show that a second scaling regime, which we call the lattice ball scaling regime, also arises and is relevant for practical applications. In this regime, the expense scales as $d^{R^2}/(R^2!)$ and therefore grows polynomially with $d$. This regime arises without additional special assumptions of special types of function spaces or error norms. The lattice ball scaling regime occurs when $R^2\ll d$, due to the discrete nature of counting the expense as the number of lattice points inside a hypersphere. Here we investigate this regime, which arises from the classical problem of approximating high-dimensional functions from common spaces of analytic or $m$-times continuously differentiable functions using orthogonal series (spectral method) such as Fourier, Chebyshev, and Legendre polynomial series. For many applications, the expense in the lattice ball scaling regime can be substantially smaller than that of the hypercube scaling regime, making accurate approximations more accessible. Numerical illustrations include classifying images of handwritten digits from the MNIST dataset and learning the solution operators of partial differential equations, such as Burgers' equation and the radiative transfer equation. The potential for connections with artificial neural networks and other machine learning methods is also discussed.

papers.name: Peak state transfer in trees and the cost of distance
papers.abstract: There is peak state transfer between vertices $u$ and $v$ in a graph $G$ if there exists a time $t$ for which $|(\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm i t M})_{u,v}|$ saturates the triangle inequality imposed by its spectral decomposition and $M$ is either the adjacency or Laplacian matrix.
